title: Compress embedded RD and GLES3 shader code to reduce binary size
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Reduces a `template_release` binary size by **2.25 MiB** for desktop/mobile platforms (between 2.2% and 3.4% size reduction), and 0.18 MiB for Web (GLES3 only, 0.6% size reduction).

This is a low-hanging fruit I had notice a while ago when playing with `bloaty`, which was brought up again today in https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/buildsystem?msg=YBmtWnkXJmvwvMWDu so I gave it a try.

## Additional information

Vertex and fragment stages are stored in a single Deflate-compressed buffer per shader and decompressed on setup. The shader code is unchanged, so cache keys should be preserved too.
Decompression time measured to 1.7 ms on Linux on my system.

Size savings:
- RD shaders: 2.06 MiB saved out of 2.50 MiB raw text (1.50 MiB from FSR2).
 - GLES3 shaders: 0.18 MiB saved out of 0.25 MiB raw text.

Minor drawback: Compressed data re-compresses worse, so zipped binaries increase by a few KiB (e.g. ~34 KiB for wasm compressed with brotli). We could opt for not compressing GLES3 on Web specifically, but it seemed overkill to me to introduce platform-specific branching.

Another option worth discussing though is not compressing GLES3 at all, and only applying this optimization to RD shaders. The GLES3 shaders aren't big and the size gains aren't much.

Note: I used AI to run a bunch of builds for different target platforms on my system and measure the size gains, as well as run some before/after comparisons to confirm that the resulting shader code is untouched after those changes.

## Zstd compression?

I also looked into using Zstd compression instead of Deflate, which should allow compressing further without increasing decompression time.

It's available natively in Python 3.14+, but requires importing `zstandard` for older Python versions.

With the current approach of one compressed buffer per shader, Zstd shaves an extra 58 KiB off the ~500 KiB we got with Deflate, which isn't much compared to justify an additional dependency or branching the compression based on the Python version IMO.

Zstd can do better though, as it supports larger window sizes than Deflate, so all shaders could be compressed together, yielding much better compression as they share a lot of common code. That would be a major refactoring so I didn't try to implement it, but synthetic compression tests suggest it could reduce the compressed shader data to around 200 KiB (vs ~500 KiB now). An extra 300 KiB off would be nice, but I don't think it's worth the added complexity at this stage. It may become if we keep adding more huge dependencies like FSR2 seems to be.
